20-02-opti-1: In 1880, a famous scientist wrote a book about how plants move.
20-02-opti-2: Charles Darwin and his son Francis watched tiny grass seedlings near a window.
20-02-opti-3: Light came from one side. In a few hours, the seedlings bowed toward it.
20-02-opti-5: He covered some tips with tiny caps. Those seedlings hardly bent at all!
20-02-opti-6: Today, seedlings on sunny windowsills still lean toward the light.
20-02-opti-7: But how can we be sure they're reaching for the light?
20-02-welcome: Our film goes back to 1880, with Charles Darwin. First, look closely at some seedlings by a window.
20-02-lesson: Today you're the plant scientist. Order a week of growth, test the light, then ride down a maze.
20-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
20-02-assign: Time to show what you know. Use the case file to name the stimulus and the response.
how-20-02-compare: Put the flashlight beside one tray and the lamp above the other: drag them, or tap each one, then tap a tray. Press Let two days pass. Then swap them and press it again.
how-20-02-det: Pick three cards, one at a time. Tap a clue you see, then pick what it is. Predict if it grew toward the light or away from it, and watch its home appear.
how-20-02-write: What caused the plant to bend, and what does that tell you about how plants survive? Use at least one of the science words under the boxes.
how-20-02-partc: Draw the same plant on Day one and Day seven, side by side. Put the window on the right. Add arrows that show which way the stem grew.
